item.title: UK lawmaker warns it’s ‘open season’ on Christians as he sounds alarm over ‘two-tier justice’
item.description: British lawmaker says it is "open season" to discriminate against Christians in the United Kingdom while Islamist preachers go free.
item.content:encoded:
A British lawmaker is sounding the alarm over what he calls "two-tier justice" against Christians in the United Kingdom, telling Fox News Digital it is now "open season" to discriminate against believers while accusing authorities of allowing extremist Islamist preachers to operate as Christian pastors face harassment and arrest.

Lord Jackson of Peterborough, vice chair of a parliamentary group focused on religious freedom, made the charge while discussing Finnish parliamentarian Päivi Räsänen, a Christian politician whose statements about marriage and sexuality have put her at the center of a years-long European battle over religious expression and free speech.

"It does say a lot about the concerns that many of us have about attacks on Christians, and two-tier justice as between Christians and other faiths, and the fact that Christians, are, it's open season to discriminate against Christians in the United Kingdom now, and that's a very regrettable position," Jackson told Fox News Digital in an interview.

CHRISTIAN SCHOOL CHAPLAIN WINS SETTLEMENT AFTER FIRING OVER LGBTQ SERMON

Räsänen said British authorities canceled her electronic travel authorization, or ETA, in July before she applied for a visa, following her recent "hate speech" conviction over passages in a church booklet discussing homosexuality, raising fresh concerns among religious freedom advocates about the consequences of the ruling.

According to ADF International, which has been representing Räsänen in litigation, Räsänen was granted a U.K. visa on Aug. 21, but not in time for her to speak in person about free speech at an event in Northern Ireland.

"Räsänen was still blocked from speaking in person about free speech at an event in Northern Ireland yesterday, since she was granted her visa too late to attend," Alliance Defending Freedom International said in an Aug. 22 X post. "Räsänen was informed at 6.45pm last night that her visa application had been successful, and at 7.30pm she spoke remotely at the event, where she mentioned she was blocked from attending in person due to her ETA being cancelled in July."

BIBLE VERSE LEADS TO TRIAL IN EUROPE. GROWING CRACKDOWN THREATENS OUR US-UK VALUES

"We do not have the same free speech protections that are available to citizens of the United States," Jackson said. "And in this case, this particular lady expressed views, traditional views based on scripture of her belief in a relationship in the eyes of God between a man and a woman, a relationship, that marriage between a man and a woman is central to societal stability, and that she was speaking what she had read in the Bible, and the fact was that activists have used her words and her sincere faith-based beliefs to attack her and to use lawfare to ensure that she is stigmatized and criminalized."

Jackson, who has served in the House of Lords, the upper house of the Parliament of the United Kingdom, since November 2022, said he believes Muslims in the country are treated differently than Christians.

"Extreme Islamist preachers being allowed to preach in parts of the United Kingdom whilst at the same time Christian pastors are being harassed and arrested on the street, that cannot stand, that's completely unacceptable," Jackson claimed.

The British lawmaker said some of his peers are working to change direction and have greater protections over free speech.

UK PASTOR SAYS HE WAS ARRESTED FOR PREACHING THE GOSPEL, SPEAKING OUT AGAINST ISLAM

"We're fighting back in parliament and outside parliament," Jackson said. "We're working with various advocacy groups such as Christian Concern, the Christian Institute and others, and we're giving legal support to those people who are under attack. Women who, for instance, don't want to undress in a changing room with transgender women, i.e. men, women who are proud to wear a crucifix or a cross at work, and they are found to be committing a so-called microaggression."

Fox News Digital reached out to the U.K. Home Office for comment.

item.title: Deadly mosquito-borne virus claims first life in major US city as cases spread
item.description: Chicago's first West Nile virus death of 2026 follows the city's rainiest summer in years, as CDPH sprays insecticide across 15 community areas.
item.content:encoded:
A Chicago resident has died from West Nile virus, marking the city’s first death linked to the mosquito-borne illness this year, according to the Chicago Department of Public Health.

Several other cases have been reported throughout Illinois.

The virus is most commonly spread to people through the bite of an infected mosquito, although the disease cycle also includes infected birds. When mosquitoes feed on infected birds, they can pick up the virus and transmit it to humans.

2 AIRPORT WORKERS ARE DEAD AFTER MALARIA CASES SHOCK OFFICIALS AT MAJOR TRAVEL HUB

"2026 has seen the rainiest summer in Chicago in years, giving mosquitoes ample opportunities to breed," CDPH Commissioner Garth Walker said in a statement.

"The best way to protect yourself from West Nile virus is to avoid mosquito bites and take measures to stop them from breeding around your home."

In an attempt to prevent infections, the CDPH has sprayed insecticide in the following community areas: Beverly, Burnside, Chatham, East Garfield Park, the Lower West Side, Morgan Park, the Near West Side, North Lawndale, O'Hare, Pullman, Roseland, South Deering, Washington Heights, West Lawn and West Pullman.

For most people, West Nile produces mild symptoms — such as fever, aches and rashes — or none at all, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

VACATION HOT SPOT FACES NEW CDC TRAVEL WARNING AS OUTBREAK CASES CONTINUE CLIMBING

In rare serious cases, the virus invades the nervous system, causing meningitis, encephalitis (swelling of the brain), paralysis or death.

People over 50 or those with compromised immune systems are at highest risk, experts caution.

"Of those who do have symptoms, about 20%, maybe 25%, will have the flu-like symptoms — fever, headache, body aches — and it’s very hard to distinguish between that and flu," Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious diseases and addiction medicine doctor and associate professor at University of Southern California Keck School of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

There are also rare, severe neuroinvasive cases, when the virus infects the brain.

"When there's inflammation that leads to meningitis or encephalitis, that's very bad," warned Evans, who is also the CEO and chief medical officer for Wellness Equity Alliance.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"So if there's ever any severe headaches, stiff neck, disorientation, vision loss, feeling like you're just really confused, and if you're over the age of 65, or have immunocompromising conditions like severe diabetes or cancers, that's when you're going to want to seek emergency management as quickly as possible."

While there are no vaccines or specific treatments for West Nile virus, there are supportive treatments.

"For the flu-like symptoms, generally speaking, if you're not over the age of 65 and you're not immunocompromised, you don't have to go to the emergency room," Evans advised.

"But if you are over the age of 65 and/or have those immunocompromising conditions, and you're starting to experience confusion, headache, stiff neck … ER immediately, [call] 911."

Avoiding mosquito bites is the first line of defense, according to Evans.

"In areas where there are a lot of mosquitoes, DEET is going to be key," he said, recommending repellents that are at least 30% DEET for adults.

In high-burden mosquito areas, he also recommends avoiding the outdoors during sundown.

Health officials also recommend wearing loose, long-sleeved clothing; applying insect repellent (especially at dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active); and ensuring that window screens are secure.

Around homes, eliminating standing water (like that found in buckets, tires and gutters) can help keep mosquitoes from breeding.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

There have been 407 reported human cases of West Nile virus in the U.S. this year, including 285 severe neuroinvasive cases and 23 deaths, according to the latest preliminary CDC data, current as of Sept. 1.

Most West Nile cases are reported in August and September.

item.title: Aryna Sabalenka fires back at reporter for asking question about partying after US Open victory
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka fired back at a reporter during her US Open press conference after a question about brand events implied she hadn't been training.
item.content:encoded:
Aryna Sabalenka was all smiles in the media center at the U.S. Open after cruising to a straight-sets victory over Polina Iatcenko on Wednesday night to punch her ticket into the third round. That is, until one media member attempted to take the focus off of tennis and put it on Sabalenka's life off the court.

The World No. 1 got into a back-and-forth with a reporter after she interrupted his question about how she was feeling in the midst of the tournament after what was a busy week leading into the year's final Grand Slam.

GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE

"You guys are, like, a joke. Parties, fun, like, why would you even say that?" Sabalenka asked after rolling her eyes. "Why would you even think about that? What kind of question is that?

"Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands, and you think that I’ve been partying, not training?"

HATERS OF FASHION ATTACK ARYNA SABALENKA WITH 'STREETWALKER' INSULT SIMPLY BECAUSE SHE WORE FISHNET AT US OPEN

The reporter tried to clarify the question to fellow media members in the room, making note that they weren't suggesting the Belarusian had been partying, but simply pointing out that there are many events that brands and other outlets host that big-name players attend.

Sabalenka, however, wasn't having it.

"Oh yeah, I wasn’t serious before that," Sabalenka said, sarcastically. "Next question. Think before you say stuff."

Sabalenka has shared three pieces of branded content since arriving in New York on her Instagram account, but she also hasn't come close to dropping a set in each of her first two matches in Queens. The 28-year-old is also looking to win what would be her third consecutive US Open title this month, and as a two-time defending champion, media appearances and brand opportunities are a part of the experience.

Sabalenka took down American Amanda Anisimova in straight sets at the 2025 U.S. Open final, and accomplished the same against American Jessica Pegula the year prior. The Miami, Florida, resident has been atop the women's ATP rankings since October 2024.

item.title: 'Deadpool' star Ryan Reynolds torches 1980s nostalgia, calls decade a ‘f---ing mess’ people ‘forget’
item.description: Ryan Reynolds called the 1980s a "brutal" and "f---ing mess" at the "Mayday" premiere, sparking fierce pushback from Spencer Pratt and Dan Bongino.
item.content:encoded:
Ryan Reynolds faced backlash Thursday after the "Deadpool" star called the 1980s "brutal" and a "f---ing mess" while promoting his Cold-War era movie "Mayday" at its New York premiere, prompting critics to question his characterization of the decade and the contrast with his nostalgia-driven new film.

Reynolds said modern nostalgia can obscure the darker realities of distinct periods in history, including the decade depicted in his latest movie.

"When you get far enough away from a time period that’s quite distinct, there’s always a lovely feeling associated with it, almost like you pave over all the trauma with puppy dogs and ice cream," Reynolds said in an interview with Variety. "The 80s was a brutal, brutal time for people. It was a f---ing mess and people forget that."

RYAN REYNOLDS STARS AS SHOT-DOWN NAVY PILOT RESCUED BY EX-KGB AGENT IN APPLE TV+’S ‘MAYDAY’

Christian Toto, an award-winning film critic and founder of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital on Thursday that Reynolds’ comments were especially striking because "Mayday" itself embraces the era Reynolds criticized.

"His '80s comments are so stunning. First, he was living in Canada during the 1980s and was pretty young at the time — he's 49 now, meaning in 1986 he was just 9 years of age," he said. "Much more importantly, his new movie 'Mayday' is a love letter to the 1980s. It doesn't describe the decade as perfect, but it's a perfectly sweet nostalgia blast atop a buddy comedy template. Why he would trash the decade, ignoring its joyous spirit and all-American vibe, is a mystery."

"Ryan Reynolds is one of the best marketers in Hollywood. And he happens to be an A-list actor, too. His business savvy is unusual, and he personally helped make the 'Deadpool' series a smash via a series of clever comic shorts. He's funny and self-deprecating, too, which never hurts," he added.

Lisa Cusack, president of the Don’t L.A. My Burbank PAC and a Los Angeles GOP delegate, told Fox News Digital on Thursday that Reynolds’ criticism overlooked what she viewed as the economic and cultural gains of the Reagan-era 1980s.

"Setting aside the fact that anyone could hate on the decade that produced ‘Back to the Future’ and ‘Indiana Jones’, the ‘80s left behind the high inflation and social unrest of the ’70s," she said. "The GDP grew and poverty rates declined. Everyone wanted to move to California and Hollywood was thriving. We don’t want to go back, but the Reagan '80s is actually a pretty good example of how there’s always a way to leave bad ideas behind and make positive progress."

HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER BEHIND 'APOLLO 13' REJECTS POLITICS IN HIS MOVIES, SEEKS TO UNITE AUDIENCES

Television personality Spencer Pratt, who has publicly advocated for bringing film and television production jobs back to the United States, responded to Reynolds by tying the comments to Hollywood's relationship with American audiences.

"Here I am trying to bring back American film jobs, and then these tools keep saying stupid crap like this and making every normal American hate them. Hollywood is seriously its own worst enemy. Just stick to the Cricket wireless ads, dude," Pratt said on X.

Fox News Digital reported this week that the U.S. entertainment industry has lost 49,000 jobs since 2022, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data, as productions increasingly shifted to competing states and overseas locations. In Los Angeles, where Pratt recently ran for mayor, scripted television production in the region was down nearly 30% from 2019 and more than 80 production-service businesses had closed since 2022 amid reduced production and industry strikes.

TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS

Dan Bongino also pushed back on Reynolds’ description of the decade, pointing to the 1980 "Miracle on Ice," the fall of the Berlin Wall, economic growth under former President Ronald Reagan and the era’s popular culture.

"This dude doesn’t know jack s--- about the 1980s in America — and Jack left town. I was a teenager when the ’80s ended, and it was an INCREDIBLE time to be alive. No social-media rage farming," Bongino said on X. "The Miracle on Ice kicked off the decade, and the Berlin Wall and communism came crashing down at the end. Reagan putting up monster GDP growth numbers. Pre-woke MTV. ‘Indiana Jones’."

"No men in women’s bathrooms. And much, much more. The ’80s TORE IT UP. Friends don’t let friends fall for Hollywood propaganda. God bless America—and God bless the ’80s!" he added.

item.title: Former NFL player and college football star dead after final social media post claiming demonic possession
item.description: Alphonso Smith's final social media post referenced demon possession and childhood abuse, serving as a haunting cry for help hours before his death.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Former NFL cornerback Alphonso Smith Jr. was found dead in a Florida community on Wednesday mere hours after he is believed to have authored a self-loathing and lamentable post on social media that suggested he was a victim of child abuse and demonic possession.

The last line of the troubling post warned: "This is it."

A family member who did not wish to be publicly identified confirmed to OutKick that Smith, 40, is dead. The cause of death has not been confirmed. TMZ reported that Smith died by suicide, but OutKick could not independently verify the report.

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION JORDAN DEVEY DEAD AT 38 BY SUICIDE

Whatever the manner in which Smith died, it is clear his final Facebook post was a cry requiring help.

"Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME!," Smith wrote.

"I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It's EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it!

"I am so sorry! I am a piece of sh*t! It's a lot of you that are! I am A COWARD! A HUGE COWARD!

"I am so sorry…"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Part of Smith's note addresses his friends and family, including his children, in what appears to be something of a goodbye.

"To my kids, daddy is SO SORRY!" he posted.

"To my friends, I love you all, but your boy was f*cked up!

"To my family, BABY, my MOM, my siblings, things happened to your boy, your brother while I was little that an older lady did onto me. As a result guys, I did the same onto others!

"Please forgive me!"

"Please pray over your families! PLEASE PRAY FOR ALL I've affected!"

Smith obviously did a lot of self-reflection before writing this note and clearly found himself lacking. What exactly he was referring to remains unclear.

FORMER COWBOYS DEFENDER MARSHAWN KNEELAND, WHO DIED BY SUICIDE AT 24, FOUND TO HAVE EARLY STAGE CTE

"I am the WORST & I pray my soul rest in heaven for my heart is pure, but my BRAIN & experience is MESSED UP!!" Smith wrote.

"Once again to ALLLLLL! I am SORRY! THIS IS IT!"

The stranger part of all this is that the day prior to his post, Smith is caught on video knocking on the door of a nearby home and offering to buy everyone breakfast. And last year, he spoke to the Wake Forest football team.

Smith, born in Pahokee, Florida, was a standout defensive back at Wake Forest, where he set the school record with 21 interceptions.

The Denver Broncos selected him in the second round of the 2009 NFL Draft (37th overall) but traded him to the Detroit Lions after his rookie season.

Smith played 42 games with 11 starts during his four-year NFL career. He finished with 88 tackles and eight interceptions and perhaps some lingering personal pain.

item.title: Steel Across America tour lands at Fenway Park ahead of 25th anniversary of 9/11
item.description: The 21-foot World Trade Center steel beam drew emotional reactions at Fenway Park as fans shared deeply personal connections to the 9/11 attacks.
item.content:encoded:
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour landed at Boston's Fenway Park Wednesday night, giving Red Sox fans a chance to see a preserved section of the World Trade Center.

The 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center has been on a tour across America since May, and it is scheduled to finish its journey in New York City just after Sept. 11.

"It brings up a lot of memories, and, honestly, reading that and talking to the firemen over there, it can give me chills. It gives me chills," Fenway vendor David Littlefield said of the display.

WHERE TUNNEL TO TOWERS' STEEL ACROSS AMERICA TOUR WILL STOP AHEAD OF 9/11

"It was gut-wrenching, heartbreaking," he said, adding that his wife lost a roommate in the attacks.

"It hits home. I worked for American Airlines for 30 years, and I … worked Flight 11 and Flight 77 many times," another woman at the game said.

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

The display is now being featured at the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial on Thursday.

The 16,900-pound beam will then head to the nation's capital, where it will be featured at a private event on Friday. It will then head to New York City for another private event in Brooklyn on Sept. 11, before a final appearance at the New York Giants vs. Dallas Cowboys game at MetLife Stadium Sept. 13.

NFL TO COMMEMORATE 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF 9/11 TERRORIST ATTACKS ACROSS ALL ITS STADIUMS AND EVEN IN AUSTRALIA

The beam visited the U.S. Military Academy at West Point on Monday, where the superintendent, Lt. Gen. James B. Bartholomees III, said the piece of steel connects the courage shown by first responders on 9/11 with the Americans who answered the call to serve in the years that followed.

"As we approach the 25th anniversary of 9/11, this piece of steel reminds us of the courage of first responders like Stephen Siller and the countless Americans who answered the call in the years that followed, including generations of West Point graduates," Bartholomees said. "Today, young men and women continue that legacy of service, guided by duty, honor country."

The ceremony brought together cadets, faculty, staff and guests and opened with a color guard and pipe and drum procession by members of the NYPD, FDNY and Port Authority Police Department. The program also included the national anthem, an invocation and blessing of the steel and a moment of reflection accompanied by "Amazing Grace."

item.title: 'Sopranos' star Dominic Chianese continues to age in reverse, starts podcast at 95 years old
item.description: Dominic Chianese launched "Dominic & Junior" with his son, reflecting on his legendary career from "The Godfather Part II" to Junior Soprano.
item.content:encoded:
If any of you loyal readers are lucky enough to still have grandparents alive, congratulations.

And if any of those grandparents are still kicking at the ripe age of 95, congratulations again.

With all that being said, I doubt few if any of those 95-year-old grandparents are starting a podcast, but that's exactly what former "Sopranos" star Dominic Chianese has decided to do as his next career move.

'THE SOPRANOS' ACTOR VINCENT PASTORE DEAD AT 80

The man who played Corrado "Junior" Soprano and gave us such classic lines as "he never had the makings of a varsity athlete" as well as other expressions my editors won't let me put in print is teaming up with his son, Dominic Jr. (ironically enough), to deliver a podcast reflecting on the elder Chianese's career in Hollywood, including his turn as the boss of New Jersey's bespectacled uncle.

"I’m 95 now. I’ve been thinking a lot about (legacy), especially since I’m going to be talking to millions of people," Chianese told People.

"To be honest with you, I was a little frightened because I thought millions of people are going to hear what’s coming out of my mouth. That’s serious stuff," he said.

"And [my son] said, ‘Don’t worry, Pop, everything’s okay.’"

HOW TO WATCH THE 'HANG OUT WITH SEAN HANNITY' PODCAST

"Sopranos" actors and podcasting seem to go hand in hand, as Chianese isn't the only one from the show to try his hand in the medium.

Steve Schirippa and Michael Imperioli, who played Bobby Bacala Jr. and Christopher Moltisanti, respectively, famously started their "Talking Sopranos" podcast during COVID and even featured Chianese on an episode.

‘SOPRANOS’ STARS REUNITE IN EMOTIONAL FAREWELL FOR VINCENT PASTORE

The Soprano children even got in on the podcast fun, as Jamie-Lynn Sigler and Robert Iler (Meadow and A.J. Soprano) have a podcast of their own called "Not Today, Pal."

Chianese is obviously best known for his role in the HBO hit mob series, but his acting career spans over half a century and includes roles in other gangster classics like "The Godfather, Part II" and "Boardwalk Empire."

The first episode of the podcast, titled "Dominic & Junior" dropped on Sept. 1.

Even though "The Sopranos" hasn't been on the air in almost 20 years, Chianese looks as young and as vibrant as he did the day the series wrapped.

HOW 'SOPRANOS' STAR VINCENT PASTORE HELPED CREATE THE SINGLE GREATEST TELEVISION SEASON OF ALL TIME

It's incredible to see a man his age still doing what he loves, and "Sopranos" fans will be happy to know that their favorite TV uncle still holds the show and his role in such high regard.

Just don't mention anything about his trips to Boca.

item.title: Reactions pour in after HBO drops new trailer for its upcoming Harry Potter mega-series
item.description: HBO's "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" series drops a new full trailer with a star-studded cast including John Lithgow and Nick Frost.
item.content:encoded:
A new full trailer is out for HBO's upcoming Harry Potter series, and reactions are rolling in.

Here's the basic info:

'DUNE: PART THREE' TRAILER IGNITES FAN FRENZY AHEAD OF THE TRILOGY-CLOSING DECEMBER 2026 RELEASE

A preview for the upcoming mega-series from HBO based on J.K. Rowling's books and the movie franchise dropped back in March, and hype has been deafening ever since the show was first announced.

It'd be shocking if that weren't the case.

"Harry Potter" is arguably the most commercially successful book series ever written, and the films took things to a different level.

'THE TERMINAL LIST' SEASON 2 FIRST PREVIEW DROPS WITH CHRIS PRATT RETURNING AS NAVY SEAL JAMES REECE

Now, HBO is getting in on the action with a series. Every season will focus on a single book, which allows for a more in-depth journey.

A new preview was released Wednesday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

It didn't take long after the preview was released for reactions to roll in on social media. Check out some of the reactions below.

Personally, I'm cautiously optimistic. Is this series necessary? Absolutely not. Will I still watch it? Without a second of hesitation.

The biggest positive is that the series will be able to go much deeper than the movie, which were all great. The pivot to darkness in the third book and movie is what made Rowling's work ascend into rarefied air.

The biggest downside is that expectations are through the roof, and anything less than excellence will be a massive disappointment.

Viewers will find out starting December 25, 2026. Hit me with your predictions at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

item.title: DOJ charges ICE officer with lying to investigators following Minneapolis shooting of Venezuelan man
item.description: ICE agent Christian Castro faces federal false statements charges tied to the shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis during an immigration crackdown.
item.content:encoded:
Federal prosecutors have charged a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer with lying to investigators about the events surrounding the shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis earlier this year, Fox News Digital has learned.

The Department of Justice has charged ICE agent Christian Castro with making false statements connected to the Jan. 14 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, who was shot in the leg. He was indicted by a federal grand jury in Minnesota on Wednesday, a source familiar with the charges said.

Castro is accused of opening fire through the front door of a Minneapolis home, hitting Sosa-Celis, and then lying about the events before the shooting. The incident came amid the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration in Minnesota.

ICE OFFICER CHARGED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING RELEASED IN TEXAS AFTER JUDGE DECLINES TO INTERVENE

What followed was at least one night of unrest in Minneapolis.

The charges came after Castro was released from a Texas jail last week, following Texas Gov. Greg Abbott's refusal to sign an extradition warrant to hand him over to Minnesota authorities.

Under Texas law and barring extradition, Castro must be released after 90 days of detention. Last month, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison filed an unsuccessful request for a temporary restraining order in an effort to block Castro’s release or to order his return to Minnesota, The Associated Press reported.

ABBOTT TAUNTS FAR-LEFT AG WITH FIERY WARNING OVER ICE EXTRADITION FIGHT: 'SUCH BAD LAWYERS'

Castro is charged separately in that state with assault and false reporting of a crime related to the same shooting.

Federal authorities initially accused Sosa-Celis and another man of beating an officer with a broom handle and a snow shovel during a confrontation.

ICE SAYS OFFICER SHOT AND KILLED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO TRIED TO RAM HIM WITH CAR IN HOUSTON

However, the charges were dropped after video evidence showed the officers may have lied about the encounter, prompting an investigation.

On Wednesday, ProPublica reported that federal prosecutors were barred by officials in Washington from pursuing civil rights charges against Castro.

Fox News Digital has reached out to ICE, the Department of Homeland Security and the Justice Department for comment.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Duran Duran singer Simon Le Bon and wife Yasmin soak up the sun on their Italian getaway
item.description: Simon Le Bon and Yasmin Le Bon were photographed enjoying a beach day and boat outing in Sardinia, showcasing their enduring romance of 40 years.
item.content:encoded:
Duran Duran band member, Simon Le Bon, was spotted enjoying a sun-kissed European vacation with his wife.

Simon, 67, and his wife, Yasmin Le Bon, 61, were recently photographed while out and about on a beach day in Sardinia.

The musician was spotted in a pair of red swim shorts, which he paired with a white V-neck T-shirt, opting to wear it for parts of their stroll — and letting it hang around his neck during the rest.

His wife stunned in a classic black string bikini.

JULIANNE HOUGH FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS AS SHE SHARES SNAPS FROM HER TRIP TO SARDINIA

Some of the photos showed the couple walking alongside one another on the coastline, while others featured them cooling off with a dip in the ocean, standing in knee-deep water with their friends.

In other photos, the two joined their friends on a boat. Yasmin was photographed sunbathing with a friend, while Simon helped steer the boat, before they both jumped off and took a swim together.

The couple met in 1984 after Simon saw a cover featuring Yasmin in the portfolio of photographer Mike Owen and asked him for her number. He then contacted her and asked her to accompany him to the premiere of "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom."

While they started out as friends, their relationship blossomed into a romance when they reconnected in Paris in 1985. They were engaged sometime that year and tied the knot in December 1985.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I wake up in the morning and for ten minutes or so I just get to look at her sleeping peacefully. That's kind of all you need to know about me," he told the Daily Mirror in December 2010. "I guess I'm very lucky that I picked somebody really bloody good in the first place! She's great fun, fantastic, beautiful and we laugh all the time. It's not always easy at all. But I really want to stay married for life."

Simon found fame as the lead vocalist for the iconic British pop-rock band, Duran Duran, which also included Nick Rhodes, John Taylor, Roger Taylor and Andy Taylor.

The band formed in 1978 and shot to global stardom in 1982 with the release of their album "Rio," which featured hits such as "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Save a Prayer."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Together the bandmates have won two Grammy Awards and two BRIT Awards and were honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. In 2022, the band was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

They continue to make music together now, having released their song, "Free To Love," featuring Nile Rodgers, in April 2026.

"We carry on, you know. Not just because we’ve got a point to make with the band," he told Stereogum in November 2021. "We've made great music. We love the music that we make together. We get the same thrill, when we discover that new bassline or that melody or that beat or those keyboards. We get the same thrill of creation that we got 40 years ago."

item.title: Lawmakers press DHS in letter over Chinese forced labor allegations, flag popular Labubu dolls
item.description: The House CCP Committee demands a DHS briefing on enforcing the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act as Chinese goods from slave labor reach U.S. markets.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX — The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is requesting a briefing from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on the agency's implementation of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA), a law designed to combat the import of Chinese goods made with slave labor, according to a letter shared exclusively with Fox News Digital.

The UFLPA, passed in 2021, directed DHS' Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force to develop a strategy for quelling the importation of goods into the United States that are "manufactured wholly or in part with forced labor in the People's Republic of China."

Human rights groups began shining a spotlight on the alleged oppression and forced labor the CCP was imposing on Uyghurs, a Muslim ethnic minority in China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR), a sparsely populated Chinese territory in the country's far west.

MOTHER RECOUNTS HORRORS OF BRUTAL CHINESE DETENTION CAMP WHERE INFANT SON DIED

"The Uyghurs are being politically persecuted in Xinjiang, China. They are being forced to give up their religion. They're being forced to assimilate into Chinese culture. And many of them are being forced to do labor, to work for low wages or no wages and long hours," Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., the ranking member on the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview.

Khanna argued that enforcement of the UFLPA is not just a moral issue, but one of economic and national security for Americans.

KHANNA DEMANDS ANSWERS FROM CCP-LINKED COMPANY ACCUSED OF UNDERCUTTING US MANUFACTURERS

"This is a human rights violation, but the broader problem also for Americans is that they're making steel, they're making aluminum, they're making textiles, and then they're dumping it into the U.S. market. How could U.S. Steel or Cleveland Cliffs or our aluminum manufacturers compete with slave labor? Of course we can't. So what our letter does is it says that we need more of these companies that are using forced Uyghur labor to be designated by the Department of Homeland Security," Khanna continued.

The bipartisan letter, addressed to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asks the agency to address 10 concerns the committee has, including what work DHS and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) are doing to update the list of companies and entities on the UFLPA Entity List.

GSA FINDS CHINA-MADE TECH LABELED 'MADE IN USA' IN FEDERAL PROCUREMENT PROGRAM, ORDERS SWEEPING REVIEW

DHS added an additional 43 companies to the list in July, an action that Khanna applauded.

"I think the administration may have gotten wind that we were doing this letter and that precipitated action. You know, for a year, they hadn't done anything. Now, I give them some credit for having 44 of these companies on the list. But hopefully, once the letter goes out, we'll see more action," he said.

CHINA’S ROUTING OF BIDEN IN CHIP WAR WITH US CREATED A COMMUNIST TECH GIANT

The committee's letter highlights concerns that products produced by companies on the list and that are coming from the XUAR are still making their way to U.S. customers. Those products, the letter alleges, cover supply chains ranging from steel and aluminum to silicon-carbon materials critical to technology production.

The letter highlights a New York Times report that suggests the cotton contained in popular "Labubu" dolls comes from slave labor.

THE CCP’S NEW ‘UNITY’ LAW TURNS CHINA’S REPRESSION INTO A GLOBAL THREAT

"A lot of the textiles are coming, they come from China, are coming from Uyghurs. It's one of the easiest places to force people into labor, and that's why we included it, because of the reports that Uyghurs are involved in textile production," Khanna added.

Khanna also explained how China circumvents the import bans by outsourcing manufacturing.

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

"It's very challenging. I mean, obviously, conventionally, China has been evading some of the tariffs and protections by having their companies open up in Malaysia or Vietnam. Here, of course, you've got actual slave labor. And so what we're saying is identify these products back to the source. And if the source of the textile or steel or aluminum is forced Uyghur labor, then that should not be in the United States," he told Fox News Digital.

Ultimately, Khanna stressed, the problem of forced labor in China is a bipartisan issue, a statement seemingly reflected by the fact that the letter was signed by eight lawmakers, four Republicans and four Democrats.

CHINESE ESPIONAGE STEALS $600 BILLION FROM US FIRMS YEARLY. IT’S TIME FOR GOVERNMENT TO ACT

"This is about fair trade and human rights. Americans aren't concerned about fair competition. If China had laborers that were being paid a fair wage and they were making something and we wanted to buy from them and they weren't dumping, and if China were buying from us, that would be fine. But what can't happen is them using slave labor, undercutting our market and our companies, and then not allowing our companies to sell to them. That's just not fair," he told Fox News Digital.

"Most Americans believe in trade, but they want fair trade and they don't want to be competing with slave labor," Khanna concluded.

Fox News Digital contacted the Department of Homeland Security, Customs and Border Protection, the Chinese Embassy in the U.S., and Pop Mart, the maker of Labubu, for further comment.

item.title: Cubs reliever Trent Thornton suffers epic dugout meltdown after being removed from game
item.description: Trent Thornton spiked his glove and screamed after being pulled from the mound during the Chicago Cubs' loss to the Milwaukee Brewers at Wrigley Field.
item.content:encoded:
No ifs, ands or buts about it: Chicago Cubs relief pitcher Trent Thornton was not happy with his performance.

During the top of the fifth inning of the Cubs’ 9-5 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night at Wrigley Field, Thornton was removed from the game and was fuming.

Thornton entered the game in the top of the fourth inning with a man on third and two outs with the Cubs trailing 6-5. The 32-year-old did his job and struck out Luis Lara to neutralize the scoring threat.

After the Cubs didn’t score in the bottom of the fourth inning, Thornton went out to pitch the top of the fifth inning, and things didn’t go quite as smoothly. He struck out Christian Yelich to begin the frame but then allowed three straight baserunners.

Thornton walked Joey Ortiz and allowed singles to Cooper Pratt and Jackson Chourio before being promptly removed from the game by manager Craig Counsell. That’s when Thornton snapped.

He walked into the dugout, took a few paces and then let loose. Thornton pulled off his best Rob Gronkowski impression and spiked his glove into the bench before screaming "F---!" twice.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

While Thornton was upset, his woes in the top of the fifth inning did not come back to hurt him. Ryan Rolison came on in relief of Thornton and was able to retire the next two hitters in order to keep the score at 6-5.

Thornton is in his first season with the Cubs and has been a strong reliever for the team. In 44 games, he has a 3.40 ERA in 45 innings pitched and has three saves.

Unfortunately for the Cubs, they didn’t score for the rest of the game and ultimately lost 9-5, dropping the third game of a pivotal four-game series with their National League Central rivals.

The Cubs (78-62) will try to earn a series split against the Brewers (87-53) on Thursday at 7:15 p.m. ET after dropping two of the first three games of the series.

item.title: Feds bust LGBT podcaster, former Christian reality TV star for alleged threats to kill Trump
item.description: Benjamin Azariah Southworth allegedly posted videos calling for President Donald Trump's assassination and targeted the family of his attorney.
item.content:encoded:
A prominent LGBT podcaster who formerly hosted a Christian reality television show was arrested by federal agents in Los Angeles Thursday for allegedly threatening to kill President Donald Trump.

Benjamin Azariah Southworth, 40, was indicted by a grand jury on federal charges for cyberstalking, making harassing interstate calls and threatening to kill President Trump, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli announced on X.

He said that Southworth led a harassment campaign against the family of one of Trump's personal attorneys.

TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH

"Southworth is charged with posting videos calling for President Trump’s assassination, then targeted the family of the President’s personal attorney by publishing their home address and phone numbers, and leaving voicemails threatening 'justice comes to your door," Essayli said.

The act of publicly revealing personal information of public officials and celebrities without their consent is known as "doxxing" and is usually done with the intent to harass, shame or cause harm.

"Threats against the President of the United States are federal crimes. We will not tolerate threats of political violence in the United States. My office will prosecute anyone who crosses that line to the fullest extent of the law," the U.S. attorney wrote in a statement on X.

On Southworth's website "Holy Menace," which is still live at time of publication, the podcaster sells $5 stickers that say "Kill Trump."

While being taken into custody by agents, Southworth yelled, "Donald Trump is a pedophile. The country has fallen!" according to the New York Post, which had a photographer present at the time of his arrest.

Court documents obtained by the publication allegedly state that on April 7, 2026, Southworth posted a video on his Instagram account that contained a series of threats against Trump.

"I have been vocal in calling for the execution of Donald Trump," he allegedly said. "This government is illegitimate and out of control. It’s time for course correction. Kill Donald Trump."

The documents allegedly include a myriad of other examples of Southworth making threatening comments against the president, but the papers are not publicly available.

MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY POSTING GRUESOME DEATH THREATS AGAINST KRISTI NOEM, PAM BONDI ON SOCIAL MEDIA

"Anyone who engages in or endorses political violence or assassination culture must be condemned in the harshest terms possible," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital.

"They should also immediately seek psychiatric help to treat their severe and debilitating case of Trump Derangement Syndrome that has warped their brains and made them sick in the head."

In the late 2000s, Southworth hosted the Christian reality TV show "The Remix," which aired on some of the largest Christian networks in the country, including National Religious Broadcasters TV. The show featured Christian musicians and bands.

In 2008, Southworth came out as gay. He was subsequently the opening act for gay Christian singer Ray Boltz on the singer's nationwide tour in 2010.

In 2020, he started a podcast called "Yass, Jesus!'" which is described as "an interfaith and sexuality affirming comedy podcast that believes you don't have to pick between gay and God." He cohosts the show with "Mean Girls" actor Daniel Franzese, who is also gay.

Southworth could not be immediately reached for comment.

item.title: SEC files bombshell lawsuit against LSU, Lane Kiffin while pro players fight for college eligibility in court
item.description: The Southeastern Conference sued LSU, Lane Kiffin and school leaders over an alleged campaign to recruit former NFL players for college football.
item.content:encoded:
The Southeastern Conference (SEC) blitzed LSU on Thursday with a lawsuit as Commissioner Greg Sankey and others were in court over NCAA eligibility for professional athletes.

The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama Southern Division around 11:40 a.m. Central time as the hearing over eligibility got underway. 

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The lawsuit named the university, school president Wade Rousse, vice president and athletics director Verge Ausberry and head football coach Lane Kiffin as defendants. Sankey was being questioned by the plaintiffs as the SEC's lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin hit the court portal, according to OutKick's Trey Wallace, who stepped out of court in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to report.

Coincidence? Probably not.

The lawsuit alleged that the defendants "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes to play football for LSU during the 2026-27 season, including players who signed NFL contracts with the Cleveland Browns, New Orleans Saints and Tampa Bay Buccaneers."

"Defendants have also expressed their unequivocal intent to place those athletes on LSU’s official football roster and allow them to participate in football games during the upcoming season."

The SEC says in the lawsuit that while LSU and other member schools "affirmed" that professional athletes should be barred from returning to the collegiate field, the "defendants have continued to campaign to engage in willful efforts to recruit and soon roster professional athletes in direct defiance of the Professionalism rules."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

The SEC called LSU’s alleged efforts to play professional athletes "detrimental to the Conference and contrary to its core purpose" and that LSU "threatens to cause further substantial harm if not curbed."

OutKick reached out to LSU for comment.

The lawsuit was filed as athletes seek a ruling that could clear the way for them to play this fall. The SEC filed a brief in the case on Wednesday in which it stated that the question before the judge should be narrowed on whether the conference "can enforce and require its member institutions to comply with SEC rules."

Sankey provided an affidavit that stated that SEC presidents voted unanimously (15-0) in favor of the new rules with Rousse abstaining.

Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill, who also attended Thursday’s hearing, wrote in a brief that the NCAA had subjected athletes in the case to a "classic bait-and-switch."

"The NCAA's ever-changing rules have consequences beyond these individual athletes," Murrill said. "They affect the universities that recruit them, the other student-athletes with whom they compete, and the coaches and administrators responsible for complying with an increasingly complicated set of rules."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: FOX News Media announces extensive 9/11 anniversary coverage from Ground Zero, Pentagon and Shanksville
item.description: FOX News Media announces extensive 9/11 anniversary coverage with live broadcasts from Ground Zero, Washington, D.C., and Shanksville, Pennsylvania.
item.content:encoded:
FOX News Media will honor the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on America with extensive multiplatform special programming, the company announced on Thursday.

On the somber anniversary, and in the days leading up to it, Fox News personalities and correspondents will present commemorative packages and interviews while reporting live from locations across New York, Washington, D.C., and Pennsylvania.

"FOX & Friends" will spend the week of Sept. 7 broadcasting live from several locations tied to the horrific day. Co-host Steve Doocy, who was broadcasting live alongside co-host Brian Kilmeade on the morning of the attacks in 2001, will host the program’s flagship "Breakfast with Friends" series live from the historic O’Hara’s Pub in New York City just two blocks from Ground Zero.

MASSIVE PIECE OF 9/11 HISTORY MAKES STUNNING 10,500-MILE JOURNEY ACROSS AMERICA

Doocy will then travel to Washington, D.C., on Tuesday and speak with Tunnel to Towers Foundation chairman and CEO Frank Siller. The show will also feature the Steel Across America tour — a historic coast-to-coast campaign honoring those who sacrificed their lives on 9/11 — arriving at the White House.

Doocy will broadcast live from Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the crash site of United Airlines Flight 93, on Thursday.

On Friday, Fox News Channel’s special coverage will commence with "FOX & Friends" co-hosts Kilmeade, Ainsley Earhardt and Lawrence Jones broadcasting live from the Hyatt House in Jersey City, overlooking the New York City skyline. Doocy will contribute live from Ground Zero.

"America’s Newsroom" co-anchors Bill Hemmer and Dana Perino will broadcast live from Brookfield Place overlooking the World Trade Center campus in downtown Manhattan. The reading of the victims’ names from the National September 11 Memorial & Museum is also expected to air during "America’s Newsroom."

TRUMP CONFIRMS PENTAGON PLANS FOR 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF 9/11 ATTACKS, DISPUTES REPORT ON GROUND ZERO ABSENCE

"The Faulkner Focus," "Outnumbered," "America Reports" and "The Will Cain Show" will all feature special segments and interviews tied to 9/11, while Martha MacCallum’s "The Story" will report live from the Hyatt House and feature interviews with Cardinal Timothy Dolan and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch.

Throughout the day, Fox News senior correspondent Eric Shawn, who reported from Ground Zero on the day of the attacks, will contribute live from downtown Manhattan and correspondent Alexis McAdams will report live from Shanksville.

Chief national security correspondent Jennifer Griffin will contribute from the Pentagon and senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy will be stationed at the White House.

On FOX Business Network, "The Claman Countdown" anchor Liz Claman will commemorate the 658 Cantor Fitzgerald employees lost in the 9/11 attacks on Sept. 10. The following day, Claman will feature an interview with Silverstein Properties CEO Larry Silverstein from the World Trade Center, which he helped rebuild following the attacks.

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

Fox News Digital will publish multiple retrospective and feature stories focused on survivors, first responders, victims’ families and those carrying the legacy of 9/11 forward 25 years later. Fox News Digital will also provide day-of coverage of the commemorations at Ground Zero, the Pentagon and Shanksville, including livestream embeds from all three ceremonies.

Fox News Digital will also feature interviews with National September 11 Memorial & Museum CEO Elizabeth L. Hillman and former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill, among others. The platform will publish a "Never Forget" archival photo retrospective, including a look at how Ground Zero and the Manhattan skyline have changed since the attacks.

FOX Nation will debut two new specials ahead of the anniversary, starting with "Paul Mauro’s Notes from Ground Zero" on Sept. 4. The special spotlights Fox News contributor and former NYPD Inspector Paul Mauro, who was working the morning of 9/11 and scribbled down notes in the days following the attacks, as he returns to Ground Zero for the first time in 25 years.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

On September 8, FOX Nation will launch "Born on 9/11: 25 Years with Harris Faulkner," exploring the lives of people born on September 11, 2001. FOX Nation will also livestream the official ceremonies at the NYC memorial site and the Pentagon next Friday.

FOX News Audio and FOX News Podcasts will present extensive coverage of the anniversary as well, including an eight-part documentary series entitled "FOX News Rewind: 9/11," that features a variety of Fox News personalities.

On YouTube, "The Brian Kilmeade Show" will provide access to some of Kilmeade’s most notable 9/11 interviews and affiliates will be offered an anniversary special from Kilmeade that reflects on how America has evolved over the last 25 years.

item.title: Blue state governor candidate claims he ‘met Satan in person’ in resurfaced podcast episode
item.description: Colorado Republican Victor Marx claimed on his podcast he "met Satan in person" while praying for a girl at a high-security Texas youth prison.
item.content:encoded:
Colorado's Republican gubernatorial nominee claimed in a resurfaced podcast episode that he "met Satan in person" through another person.

Talking Points Memo first reported that Colorado GOP gubernatorial nominee Victor Marx, a Marine veteran and Christian ministry leader, claimed in a 2020 episode of his podcast, "I’ve met the devil" and "I’ve met Satan in person, through a person."

According to Marx’s account on his podcast, the encounter occurred when he was praying for a girl in a high-security youth prison in Texas. He said, "This girl started manifesting a demon" and emphasized, "it was so real that all the other locked up girls, all the other gang members, man, they all kind of huddled in a corner."

Marx described the encounter as "horrible," saying, "This demon… just really manifested pretty nasty." He said that when he asked the demon its name, it responded, "I am Satan." He added, "If you think I’m joking, I’m not."

TRUMP-APPOINTED JUDGE BLOCKS BLUE STATE'S CRACKDOWN ON ICE DETENTION CENTER

Though Marx described the little girl as "just adorable," he said he could tell "she had a demon in her."

"All of a sudden, this demon goes, ‘I guess you’re going to say I’m possessed.’ And I just — I just started laughing," said Marx, adding, "I was like, ‘I don’t think I have to. It’s kind of obvious.’ I mean, really, that’s — I just snickered, which makes the devil mad."

Marx is the founder of All Things Possible Ministries, a Christian ministry whose website says it is devoted to "setting captives free spiritually, emotionally and physically."

'GHOST TOWN?' COLORADO BUSINESS LEADERS WEIGH ALL OPTIONS AS DSA GAINS GROUND

After winning the GOP gubernatorial nomination earlier this summer, Marx made headlines for assembling an all-Marine ticket that he said can bring the "steely spines" needed to combat a democratic socialist movement gaining ground in races around the country. He is pitching himself and his running mate, retired Marine Col. George Markert, as political outsiders, arguing that they have the discipline and accountability needed to take on the movement.

He has built his long-shot campaign around public safety, social conservatism and the cost of living. The campaign comes as the Democratic Party's left flank scored a series of primary wins nationally, including in Colorado, where democratic socialist Melat Kiros upset longtime incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette.

Marx is running against Democrat Phil Weiser, the attorney general of Colorado who is favored to win the race to succeed Gov. Jared Polis, another Democrat who is term-limited.

Fox News Digital's Ashley J. DiMella contributed to this report.

item.title: Mamdani gives influencers special access as Signal use raises records-law questions
item.description: Zohran Mamdani's City Hall uses a Signal group chat to feed talking points to 200-plus social media influencers, raising record-keeping concerns.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is giving special access to a network of approximately 200 social media influencers who take City Hall talking points and videos to promote municipal programs online to residents, according to a new report.

The report, by the Columbia Journalism Review, highlights that the online personalities get their talking points through an encrypted Signal group text, called "NYC Creators Announcements."

Signal offers a disappearing-messages feature that can automatically delete messages after a set period of time if enabled. It is unclear whether that feature is active in the Mamdani administration’s group, raising questions about compliance with city record-keeping laws.

Questioned by reporters whether the use of Signal possibly breaks city laws, Mamdani said, "My administration will always strive to fully comply with all legal requirements, including those that relate to the preservation of city records."

THIS IS WHAT MAMDANI JUST BANNED FOR NEW YORK CITY STUDENTS IN ELEMENTARY AND MIDDLE SCHOOLS

"If there are any departures from what is legally required, my administration will look into it immediately and take corrective action," Mamdani added on Wednesday.

The use of Signal for government communications made major headlines last year, when then-Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth came under fire after sensitive, real-time details about U.S. military strikes were shared in a Signal group that included a journalist.

The Columbia Journalism Review report also said influencers are not paid by the city for participating in the group or for their coverage, although some receive payments from marketing and advertising firms with contracts from city agencies for work on specific messaging campaigns. The municipal programs promoted include voting, healthcare, immigration and tenants’ rights, participatory budgeting and composting.

HEAD HERE FOR THE LATEST FOX NEWS REPORTING ON NYC MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI

City employees told researchers the payments to influencers for their work ranged from $5,000 to $20,000 per campaign, according to the report.

The Signal group was formed out of Creators4Zohran, a group that supported Mamdani’s 2025 mayoral campaign. Mamdani rocked the political world by winning election as the first socialist mayor of the nation's most populous city.

The group chat is steered by Emilia Rowland, the New York City director of new media and cultural communications. Rowland and her staff push out daily updates, talking points, and clips that the influencers can use in their posts.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The chat operates like a traditional press list used by communications teams to send updates and information to reporters.

Cities are increasingly using influencers to promote municipal services, policies and to engage the public more directly than through traditional media.

"New Yorkers get their news in a wide variety of ways, and it is our responsibility to ensure that we communicate information from city government directly to the people of the city, whether that means to all of you, to TV, to radio, to social media, to content creators and so on and so forth," Mamdani emphasized.

Fox News Digital reached out to City Hall but didn't receive a response at the time this report was published.

item.title: GOP Sen Thom Tillis urges Trump to replace Pete Hegseth, blasts Pentagon leadership
item.description: Sen. Tillis called for President Trump to replace War Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing the Pentagon chief of "creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks."
item.content:encoded:
Outgoing Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., called for President Donald Trump to replace War Secretary Pete Hegseth, slamming the Pentagon leader following the news that Army Secretary Dan Driscoll was resigning.

"I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it," Tillis declared in a fiery Wednesday post on X.

Tillis praised Driscoll in the post — and apparently referring to ex-Army chief of staff Gen. Randy George (ret.), the senator declared, "He and General George began a transformative period of innovation in how we array our forces and equip our Soldiers. He challenged our legacy approach to manning and procurement. Most of all, he cared deeply about the men and women in our Army formations and quickly earned their respect."

But Tillis excoriated Hegseth.

"If we had a @SecWar who maintained the same priorities and forward-thinking, he would be fighting to retain talented leaders like Dan and the many flag officers he has forced into retirement. Instead, he is creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks," the senator wrote.

ARMY CHIEF OF STAFF ORDERED TO RETIRE IMMEDIATELY AS HEGSETH CONTINUES PENTAGON SHAKEUP

"I served on Senate Armed Services for 8 years and as chair or ranking member of the Personnel and Readiness subcommittee. I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force," the lawmaker declared.

Tillis, who announced last year that he would not seek re-election, told Politico Magazine earlier this year that he would "love to see Pete Hegseth fired because he's incompetent and doing a horrible job."

The War Department declined to provide comment on Thursday.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement to Fox News Digital, "After Joe Biden’s Pentagon prioritized DEI and woke ideology, President Trump and Secretary Hegseth quickly reversed course and restored a Department of War that is focused on readiness, lethality, and supporting our warfighters. The President has complete trust in Secretary Hegseth, who is doing an incredible job leading the Pentagon. The results of Operations Midnight Hammer, Absolute Resolve, Southern Spear, and Epic Fury speak for themselves."

TRUMP'S ARMY SECRETARY HUNT TAKES SHAPE AS INSIDERS FLOAT POTENTIAL PICKS

Driscoll, in a Tuesday statement issued on the official Secretary of the Army X account, noted that Wednesday would be his final full day in the position.

"As a third-generation Army veteran, it has been the honor of a lifetime to serve as the Secretary of the Army under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth. Tomorrow is my last full day in the role," Driscoll said in the statement.

"I had the privilege of working with them to modernize and accelerate how the Army mans, trains, and equips the most lethal fighting force on the face of the earth. We could not have made the progress we did without the support of Secretary Hegseth. I am forever grateful to President Trump for the opportunity to once again serve my country," he noted.

ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP

A source familiar with Driscoll's resignation indicated to Fox News that "Driscoll brought up concerns with the administration surrounding Army transformation and readiness and Hegseth's blocking those efforts specifically by firing the Generals who were responsible."

Fox News Digital's Sophia Compton and Fox News' Jennifer Griffin and Liz Friden contributed to this report.

Well there you have it. A form of romance that on paper looks like it could be lonely and have a slight scent of cat food. That couldn’t be further from how it works when practiced in the real world.

In reality, it's sleek and sophisticated, and you're the apex predator in a cat world. It's about fun and being drama free. I know that would appear to the untrained eye as if there are unresolved issues with relationships. That's silly.

There's good news on the Orgy Dome front. Burning Man will take place with its special tents fully erected. Last year's pounding took it out.

But the folks responsible for making the magic happen every year asked for help and the people came through for the Orgy Dome.

The NY Post is reporting that the "hedonist hideaway" is "back up and running." They received the donations necessary to erect it.

They're stocked up on protection, and it's a go on getting the dome rocking during this year's festival. Sure there's lost time to make up for, but not without throwing safety out the window.

"We want an atmosphere where people are playing, and not walking around staring at people, or looking at people to pick up on. A lot of our guests, they don’t want to be picked up on by singles," an organizer said of the dome.

I had originally planned to go with another story in this slot, but when this popped up this morning, I took it as a sign. I always go where the romance takes me, and today it took me to the Orgy Dome at Burning Man.

I may still, in the future, use the other story. So I'm not going to spoil it here. The return of the Orgy Dome has far too much romance in it to ignore.

On top of that, it was a slice of good news that I felt went well with the realization that you're not quite as weird as you thought you were.

You could be under the impression that your romantic preference is weird. Okay, it could be a little weird, but not as weird as you think it is.

There are a few mentioned here by the freaks on Reddit that I would never have guessed would be romantic preferences and even if there are others into them, they're still pretty damn weird.

I mean necks, veins, and hands? What is going on with that? If any of those are your romantic preferences, I need to know more about them. Here's the proof that you're not that weird:
